br.br:
1. An access cover panel assembly comprising:an inner cover plate;
an outer cover plate spaced from the inner cover plate defining a circumferentially spaced-apart plurality of apertures,
a circumferentially spaced-apart plurality of U-shaped floating nut plate assemblies dependently extending from the inner cover plate toward the outer cover plate each in alignment with a respective one of the apertures, and
a plurality of attachment bolts extending through each of the apertures of the outer cover plate and threadably coupled to a respective one of the floating nut plate assemblies to removably secure the inner and outer cover plates to one another.
2. The access cover panel assembly according to claim 1, wherein the floating nut plate assemblies comprise:a pair of circumferentially spaced-apart support legs having an upper end rigidly joined to the inner cover plate; and
a nut plate which bridges the support legs so as to be rigidly connected with lower terminal ends thereof.
3. The access cover panel assembly according to claim 2, further comprising threaded nuts each fixed to and carried by respective upper surfaces of the nut plate.
4. The access cover panel assembly according to claim 3, wherein the nut plates include an opening to allow respective attachment
bolts to extend therethrough and be threadably coupled to the threaded nuts.
5. The access cover panel assembly according to claim 2, wherein the nut plates establish a gap with an opposed inner perimetrical surface region of the outer cover plate.
6. The access cover panel assembly according to claim 1, wherein the inner cover plate includes an O-ring seal positioned at an outer peripheral edge region thereof.
7. The access cover panel assembly according to claim 6, wherein the inner cover plate includes an annular recess formed in the outer peripheral edge region of the inner cover plate, and wherein the O-ring seal is positioned within the annular recess.
8. An aircraft wing comprising:an internal fuel tank;
a lip structure defining an access opening through an external skin of the wing to allow access to the fuel tank, and
a cover plate assembly removably connected to and covering the access opening in the wing, wherein the cover plate assembly comprises:
(i) an inner cover plate;
(ii) an outer cover plate spaced from the inner cover plate defining a circumferentially spaced-apart plurality of apertures,
(iii) a plurality of circumferentially spaced-apart U-shaped floating nut plate assemblies dependently extending from the inner cover plate toward the outer cover
plate each in alignment with a respective one of the apertures, and
(iv) a plurality of attachment bolts extending through each of the apertures of the outer cover plate and threadably coupled to a respective one of the floating nut plate assemblies to thereby removably secure the inner and outer cover plates to one another and to exert a compressive force onto a surface of the lip structure.
9. The aircraft wing according to claim 8, wherein the floating nut plate assemblies comprise:a pair of circumferentially spaced-apart support legs having an upper end rigidly joined to the inner cover plate; and
a nut plate which bridges the support legs so as to be rigidly connected with lower terminal ends thereof.
10. The aircraft wing according to claim 9, further comprising threaded nuts each fixed to and carried by respective upper surfaces of the nut plate.
11. The aircraft wing according to claim 10, wherein the planar nut plate assemblies include an opening to allow respective attachment bolts to extend therethrough and be threadably coupled to the threaded nuts.
12. The aircraft wing according to claim 9, wherein the nut plates establish a gap with an opposed peripheral edge region of the outer cover plate.
13. The aircraft wing according to claim 8, wherein the inner cover plate includes an O-ring seal positioned at a peripheral edge region of the inner cover plate.
14. The aircraft wing according to claim 13, wherein the inner cover plate includes an annular recess formed in the peripheral edge region of the inner cover plate, and wherein the O-ring seal is positioned within the annular recess.
15. The aircraft wing according to claim 14, wherein the O-ring seal is sealingly compressed against an opposed surface of the lip structure defining the access opening in the external skin of the aircraft wing.
16. An aircraft which comprises the aircraft wing according to claim 8.
